name: Cricket
description: Stridulation produces species-specific chirp patterns encoding temperature data (Dolbear's Law). Phonotaxis enables sound-gradient navigation. Tympanic membranes on front legs provide directional hearing via inter-leg phase comparison.

core_attributes.neurology: tibial tympanic organs, stridulation motor pattern generator, phonotactic circuits
core_attributes.pattern: stridulation encoding, phonotactic navigation, temperature-frequency coupling

scope.definition: Information content (bits/second) of cricket chirp encoding — species, sex, condition, and temperature — calculated from neural discriminability of chirp parameters in conspecific auditory neurons.

evidence.source: Huber & Thorson (1985) 'Cricket auditory communication', Scientific American 253:60-68; Doherty (1985) 'Trade-off phenomena in calling song of black field crickets', Behaviour 94:1-22.
cross_domain_examples: field cricket chirp rate encodes temperature: 4 chirps/15 s → subtract 40 → Fahrenheit (Dolbear's Law)
female crickets discriminate species by chirp syllable interval within 2 ms resolution
frog advertisement calls: analogous multi-parameter encoding of fitness and species identity in acoustic signal

scope.falsifiability: If female crickets show equal phonotaxis toward heterospecific and conspecific calls in controlled playback experiments, chirp-pattern discrimination is not driving mate choice.
scope.measurement_limits: Encoding specificity is carrier-frequency and temperature-dependent. Chirp rate shifts 30% over 10°C range, requiring temperature compensation for species identification. Background noise masks at 10 dB above signal.

scope.definition: Accuracy of female cricket approach toward male call source — deviation from straight-line path to speaker in phonotaxis experiments — expressed as path efficiency (straight-line / actual path length).

evidence.source: Wendler et al. (1980) 'The coordination of walking leg movements in crickets', Journal of Experimental Biology 88:255-268; Hedwig & Poulet (2004) phonotaxis in Gryllus bimaculatus.
cross_domain_examples: female Gryllus approaches male call source with path efficiency 0.83-0.91 over 50 cm open arena
directional hearing via pressure-difference receiver (tympanic membranes coupled through trachea) enables 2° angular resolution
barn owl auditory localization: convergent triangulation using interaural time difference — 1-2° accuracy

scope.falsifiability: If female crickets navigate equally efficiently toward call sources in directional-cue-blocked conditions (sealed trachea), the pressure-difference receiver is not the primary directional cue.
scope.measurement_limits: Path efficiency degrades with noise from multiple simultaneous male calls. Tympanic membrane coupling to trachea only provides directional information at optimal carrier frequencies (4-5 kHz for G. bimaculatus).

scope.definition: Correlation coefficient (R²) between ambient temperature and cricket chirp rate across field populations — basis of Dolbear's Law thermometry.

evidence.source: Dolbear (1897) 'The cricket as a thermometer', American Naturalist 31:970-971; Walker (1962) 'The taxonomy and calling songs of United States tree crickets', Annals of Entomological Society America 55:303-322.
cross_domain_examples: Oecanthus fultoni (snowy tree cricket) chirp rate correlates with temperature R²=0.95 across 10-25°C
firefly flash rate: analogous temperature-biochemical coupling (Q10 ~2.0 enzyme kinetics)
enzyme reaction rate vs temperature follows Arrhenius equation — same underlying biochemistry drives chirp rate

scope.falsifiability: If chirp rate shows no statistically significant correlation with temperature across the 10-30°C range in field recordings, the temperature-biochemistry coupling model fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Correlation holds best for tree crickets — field crickets show weaker coupling (R²=0.75). Cold temperatures below 12°C produce aperiodic chirps that don't fit the linear model.
